exposure: Use of multiple antihypertensive agents (vs. one agent)
Average blood pressure (<140/90 mm Hg vs. >=140/90 mm Hg)
outcome: Antenatal admissions to rule out preeclampsia
cohort: The study included 974 singleton pregnancies with chronic hypertension from a tertiary care center.
finding: Among women with blood pressure >=140/90 mm Hg, the use of multiple antihypertensive agents was associated with a greater risk of preeclampsia, severe preeclampsia, antenatal admissions, preterm birth <35 weeks, and composite neonatal adverse outcomes, compared to a single agent.
